How much should you tip hotel housekeeping?

Unlike most tipped services, hotel housekeeping uses a flat rate per night rather than a percentage. The standard is $3–5 per night at a standard hotel and $5–10 per night at a resort or upscale property. For a 3-night stay at a mid-range hotel, budget $9–15 total.

The most important rule: tip daily, not just at checkout. Housekeeping staff rotate, meaning a different person may clean your room each day. A single tip left at checkout goes only to the last day's housekeeper. Leave $3–5 in cash on the pillow or nightstand each morning before you leave your room.

Hotel housekeeping is one of the most overlooked tipping situations in travel. Surveys suggest fewer than 30% of hotel guests leave tips. These staff clean multiple rooms per shift, often earning close to minimum wage with no guaranteed gratuity.

Factors that affect how much to tip

  • Hotel tier: Budget motel ($2–3/night), standard hotel ($3–5/night), upscale hotel ($5–7/night), luxury resort ($7–10+/night). The tip scales with the level of service expected.
  • A suite with a kitchen and living area takes a lot longer to clean than a standard double room. Tip toward the higher end for suites or rooms with multiple beds.
  • Length of stay: For extended stays (7+ nights), some guests consolidate tips to every 2–3 days rather than daily, and $10–15 per cleaning is fair.
  • Do Not Disturb usage: If you declined daily service, only tip for days the room was actually cleaned. Leave a consolidated tip at checkout for serviced days only.
  • If your room requires extra work like lots of towels, room service dishes, or a generally messier-than-average cleanup, tip toward the higher end or add a few extra dollars.

Hotel housekeeping tip etiquette

Always leave cash. Hotel housekeeping cannot be tipped via the front desk or your hotel bill in most properties. Place the tip visibly on the pillow, nightstand, or in a provided tip envelope with a note that says "Housekeeping, Thank you" so it's clear the money is intentional and not forgotten cash.

Tip separately from other hotel services: bellhop ($1–2 per bag), room service (18–20% if gratuity not included), concierge for special requests ($5–20). Each service is tipped independently.

For resort fees: even if your hotel charges a resort fee, this does not go to housekeeping staff. Continue tipping per night as normal. Resort fees cover amenities and facilities, not staff gratuity.

Frequently asked questions

How much should you tip hotel housekeeping?
Tip $3–5 per night at a standard hotel, $5–10 per night at a resort or luxury property. Leave the tip daily in cash, not just at checkout, so each housekeeper who cleans your room receives it.
Should you tip hotel housekeeping daily or at checkout?
Daily tipping is strongly preferred. Staff rotate shifts, meaning a different housekeeper may clean your room each day. Leave $3–5 cash each morning so the right person receives it.
How much do you tip hotel housekeeping for a 3-night stay?
Budget $9–15 total for a 3-night standard hotel stay ($3–5 per night). At a resort, budget $15–30 ($5–10 per night). Leave the tip each day rather than all at checkout.
Do you tip hotel housekeeping at a budget hotel?
Yes. Budget hotel staff earn low wages and tips are just as meaningful regardless of hotel tier. Tip $2–3 per night at budget properties — a small amount that makes a real difference for minimum-wage workers.
How should you leave a hotel housekeeping tip?
Leave cash on the pillow or nightstand with a note saying 'Housekeeping — Thank you' to clarify it's a tip and not forgotten money. Leave it each morning before you leave the room for the day.
Do you tip housekeeping if you use the Do Not Disturb sign?
Only tip for days the room was actually cleaned. If you used DND for most of your stay, leave a consolidated tip at checkout for serviced days — $5–10 per cleaning is appropriate.
How much do you tip at a luxury hotel or resort?
Tip $7–10 per night at a luxury hotel or resort. Some guests at five-star properties tip $10–20 per night for attentive service. The higher service standard warrants a stronger tip.
Is it rude not to tip hotel housekeeping?
Yes. Hotel housekeeping is among the most overlooked tipping situations. Staff clean multiple rooms per shift at near-minimum wage. Not tipping is common but is considered poor etiquette by hospitality industry standards.
Do you tip the same for an extended stay?
For stays over a week, tip $3–5 per night serviced. If housekeeping only comes every few days during an extended stay, tip $10–15 per cleaning visit rather than per night.
Should you tip hotel concierge or bellhop separately?
Yes — tip each service separately. Bellhop: $1–2 per bag. Concierge (for reservations or special requests): $5–20. Room service: 18–20% if gratuity not included. None of these replace the daily housekeeping tip.
